the contribution of genetic data to the genealogical measurement of the ameridian origins of french canadians

in the context of a research programme on the genetic diversity of regional populations in quebec, we measured the contribution of ameridian ancestors to the gene pool of 794 participants living in the montreal, saguenay-lac-st-jean (slsj), gaspe peninsula and north shore regions. ameridian ancestors were identified through genealogical reconstructions (balsac database) and genetic data (mitochondrial dna) using an approach relying on the joint exploitation of the two types of data. results show that more than half of the participants have at least one ameridian ancestor in their genealogy. this means that a majority of participants carry genes received from ameridian founders. however the total genetic contribution of these ancestors to the four regional groups is low, reaching less than 1% in slsj and montreal and slightly more than 1% on the north shore and in the gaspe peninsula.
